key_insight: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy can directly fingerprint and quantify grain-boundary defect species in organic halide perovskite thin films using room-temperature spectral signatures.
engineering_relevance: This offers a non-contact diagnostic for closed-loop defect passivation and quality control in perovskite solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Measure 0.3–3.0 THz spectra of SVE-fabricated OHP films.
Match intrinsic phonon peaks and GB-localized defect vibrations to a THz fingerprint library.
Use oscillator-strength analysis to quantify defect concentration and guide passivation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the 1.58 THz absorption in MAPbI3 scales linearly with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration across four perovskite compositions.
watch_item: The approach depends on building reliable material-specific THz reference libraries and may be sensitive to film fabrication, thickness, and measurement conditions.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
